findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — getLoginPredicate() calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without null-checking getConfig(); an IDP with a null config map will throw an NPE (the Objects::nonNull guard only checks the IDP itself, not its config)

[Medium/bug] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — the BROKER_PUBLIC clause is applied unconditionally, including when a specific organizationId is passed; IDPs linked to the requested organization but not marked BROKER_PUBLIC will be silently excluded from getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY, orgId) results, changing the SPI contract for all implementations

[Medium/bug] OrganizationCacheTest.java:~377 — getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal alias "alias" for all 20 created IDPs; cleanup will fail to remove any of them, leaking test data. Should be "idp-" + i

[Medium/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~247 (getForLogin, existing-query branch) — calling cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) then re-adding a new revisioned query under the same key causes the registered invalidation to evict the just-created entry at commit, defeating the cache and causing repeated invalidation storms under mixed organizationId traffic

[Medium/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (update) — invalidations (registerIDPInvalidation, registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) are registered before idpDelegate.update(model); if the delegate update throws, the caches are invalidated anyway, causing unnecessary cluster-wide invalidation

[Low/test_gap] testCacheIDPForLogin — no test covers the NPE/null-config edge case for the new predicate clause, nor the case where idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) returns null in remove() for a non-existent alias

[Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~100 (remove) — idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) is called unconditionally on every remove (bypassing the cache), adding a DB lookup even when the IDP doesn't qualify for login-cache invalidation; could be done lazily

[Medium/concurrency] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (getForLogin) — cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) uses the current cluster counter rather than a revision obtained before the DB read; with concurrent writers the new query can be added with a revision that masks a concurrent invalidation, leaving stale IDP ID sets cached until the next write

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — getLoginPredicate() calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without null-checking getConfig(); an IDP with a null config map will throw an NPE (the Objects::nonNull guard only checks the IDP itself, not its config)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds to `getLoginPredicate()` a new predicate: `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without any null-check, while the existing `Objects::nonNull` guard only ensures `idp` itself is non-null. If `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` can ever return null, this will throw an NPE when `getOrganizationId() != null` (or when evaluating the RHS). The diff does not show any guarantee that `getConfig()` is non-null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — the BROKER_PUBLIC clause is applied unconditionally, including when a specific organizationId is passed; IDPs linked to the requested organization but not marked BROKER_PUBLIC will be silently excluded from getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY, orgId) results, changing the SPI contract for all implementations

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to always require `BROKER_PUBLIC` for any IDP with a non-null `organizationId` (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`). This predicate is not parameterized by the `organizationId` passed to `getForLogin(FetchMode, organizationId)`, so it will filter out organization-linked IDPs that are not marked public even when querying for a specific organization (e.g., `getForLogin(ALL/ORG_ONLY, orgId)`). The `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` comment indicates "public" is only intended when no specific org is provided, making the unconditional filter a correctness regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~247 (getForLogin, existing-query branch) — calling cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) then re-adding a new revisioned query under the same key causes the registered invalidation to evict the just-created entry at commit, defeating the cache and causing repeated invalidation storms under mixed organizationId traffic

adjudication.rationale: In the “existing-query but missing searchKey” branch of getForLogin, the diff shows a direct call to `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` followed by `cache.addRevisioned(query, ...)` under the same key. However, the finding’s core claim—"registered invalidation" evicting the newly-added entry at commit—cannot be verified from this diff: there is no `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` in that branch, and the semantics of `invalidateObject` (whether it defers eviction until commit, or registers an invalidation) are not shown. The assertion about "defeating the cache" via commit-time eviction is therefore not grounded in the provided code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (update) — invalidations (registerIDPInvalidation, registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) are registered before idpDelegate.update(model); if the delegate update throws, the caches are invalidated anyway, causing unnecessary cluster-wide invalidation

adjudication.rationale: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, the diff shows `registerIDPInvalidation(idpById);` and the newly added `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model);` executed before `idpDelegate.update(model);`. If `idpDelegate.update` throws, these invalidations have already been registered, causing potentially unnecessary invalidation traffic. This is a real, diff-grounded concern (newly expanded invalidation scope), but it’s an inefficiency/operational concern rather than a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] testCacheIDPForLogin — no test covers the NPE/null-config edge case for the new predicate clause, nor the case where idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) returns null in remove() for a non-existent alias

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial logic that isn’t exercised by the new test. In `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` a new clause calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)`; `testCacheIDPForLogin` only creates IDPs via representations that will have a config map, so it doesn’t cover a potential null/absent-config edge. Also, `remove()` now always does `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` and proceeds even if it’s null (e.g., non-existent alias); while `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` is protected by the `Objects::nonNull` predicate, the test does not cover the non-existent-alias path at all. This is a specific test gap around newly added/changed behavior, not a proven defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:~100 (remove) — idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) is called unconditionally on every remove (bypassing the cache), adding a DB lookup even when the IDP doesn't qualify for login-cache invalidation; could be done lazily

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now unconditionally executes `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)` (and before reading the cached entry). Previously the delegate lookup only happened in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. This new unconditional call can introduce an extra underlying-store/DB lookup even when the cached entry would have been sufficient and even when `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` ends up not invalidating (e.g., IDP not qualifying for login). This is a real, diff-grounded performance concern, not a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (getForLogin) — cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) uses the current cluster counter rather than a revision obtained before the DB read; with concurrent writers the new query can be added with a revision that masks a concurrent invalidation, leaving stale IDP ID sets cached until the next write

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), when a cache entry exists but the current searchKey isn’t cached, the code invalidates the object, captures a revision (loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)), then performs a DB read, but finally writes the new IdentityProviderListQuery with cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()) instead of using the pre-read revision (loaded). If a concurrent writer invalidates the key after the DB read starts but before addRevisioned, using the current counter can assign a revision >= the invalidation, allowing the stale ID set from the earlier DB read to “win” and remain cached until another invalidation/write.
